title: Uttaradit Family Trip: 3 Days With Kids, Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A family-friendly 3-day Uttaradit itinerary in Thailand: swim at Mae Phun Waterfall, run around Sirikit Dam, pick fruit in Laplae orchards, see old temples, and try local eats like khao phan phak and mi phan. Easy driving, kids won't get bored.
keywords: Uttaradit family trip, Uttaradit with kids, Sirikit Dam, Laplae fruit orchards, Mae Phun Waterfall
h1:
Uttaradit With the Family
3 Days of Dam, Orchards, Temples & Local Food
intro: Uttaradit is easier to do with kids than you'd expect. The distances between sights are short, so you only need to hit a few spots a day. There's a waterfall the kids can wade into, a big dam with open space to run around, Laplae fruit orchards where you can taste durian and langsat straight off the tree, and old temples plus local food the grown-ups will love. We've laid this out as a 3-day, 2-night plan with enough downtime that nobody gets worn out.

blocks.html: Before we dive in, let's be honest: Uttaradit isn't a city with theme parks or kids' museums like the big cities have. What it does well is nature, local food, and an easygoing pace with no travel hassle. If your family likes relaxed drives, letting the kids splash around, tasting fruit, and meeting real village life, this place is a great fit. But if you're after thrill rides, you'll want to dial your expectations down a notch.

items: Day 1 — Into town, pay respects at the Phraya Phichai monument, eat local, then head to Laplae to swim at Mae Phun Waterfall in the afternoon
Day 2 — A full day at Sirikit Dam: wide views, cool air, room for kids to run
Day 3 — Visit a Laplae fruit orchard (if you come in fruit season), see an old temple, grab souvenirs before heading home

blocks.title: Best time to come with the family
blocks.html: If you want the kids to taste Long Laplae and Lin Laplae durian, plus langsat and longkong straight from the orchard, come around May to August, which is fruit season. For the most fun at the waterfall, go right after fresh rain when the water is clear and not running too hard.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Town center + Mae Phun Waterfall

items.activity: Arrive in Uttaradit town, check in and drop your bags
items.note: An in-town hotel is easy to get around from and makes a good base for the first two nights

items.activity: Phraya Phichai Dab Hak monument in front of the provincial hall
items.note: A wide plaza where kids can run around; the city hero's legend is a fun one to tell them

items.activity: Local lunch — try khao phan phak or mi phan from Laplae
items.note: Por Khao Phan Phak in town has been at it for over 20 years; mild flavors that kids can eat

items.activity: Drive to Laplae district and stop at Mae Phun Waterfall to let the kids swim
items.note: Open 06:00–17:30. Each tier is shallow and good for kids; bring a change of clothes

items.activity: Stroll around the falls and grab snacks at the roadside stalls
items.note: Shady and relaxed, with restaurants and souvenir shops to browse

items.activity: Head back to town, rest, find an easy dinner
items.note: No need to cram the first day; let the kids turn in early and save energy for tomorrow

blocks.text: Day 2 — A full day at Sirikit Dam

blocks.html: Sirikit Dam is in Tha Pla district, the largest earthen dam in Thailand. It blocks the Nan River to form a wide reservoir above the dam, with open views, cool comfortable air, and plenty of space for kids to run. It's a spot where a family can spend the whole day without rushing.

items.activity: Leave town and head for Sirikit Dam
items.note: About a 1-hour drive from town; good roads and a large parking lot

items.activity: Walk up to the dam crest and photograph the reservoir view
items.note: A wide viewpoint with a cool breeze; keep an eye on kids near the railings

items.activity: Walk the Chaloem Phra Kiat suspension bridge and Sumalai Garden
items.note: A shady garden with nice photo spots; an easy walk that won't tire the kids out

items.activity: Lunch at a lakeside restaurant, focused on fresh freshwater fish
items.note: Fish straight from the reservoir, firm-fleshed; order it fried or steamed for easy eating with kids

items.activity: Take a boat ride over the reservoir (if it's running that day)
items.note: Ask about the boat queue on site, and always put a life vest on the kids

items.activity: Relax by the water and watch the sun start to dip before heading back
items.note: Lovely light in the late afternoon, and a good rest stop for the kids before the drive back

blocks.text: Day 3 — Laplae orchards + old temple + souvenirs

blocks.html: On the last day you round out the Laplae experience: an orchard where the kids actually see durian and langsat on the tree, the ancient Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang, and the Laplae City Museum that tells the town's legend to the whole family, before you load up on souvenirs to take home.

items.activity: Visit a Laplae fruit orchard and taste durian, langsat and longkong off the tree
items.note: Fruit season runs May–Aug, when many orchards open to visitors; call ahead to check before you go

items.activity: Laplae City Museum to hear the legend of the town
items.note: The 'never tell a lie' town legend keeps kids hooked and teaches a bit of local life

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang, the old temple of the town
items.note: An ancient chedi and a peaceful setting; dress modestly

items.activity: A closing lunch, then buy souvenirs — khao kaep and langsat
items.note: Khao kaep keeps well and makes an easy souvenir to bring home
Leaving in the afternoon lets the kids nap in the car and gets you home before it's too late

blocks.text: Local eats the family should try

blocks.html: Uttaradit food, especially in Laplae, has local dishes that are hard to find elsewhere, with mild flavors that work for kids on several counts. Here's what we'd suggest trying during the trip.

items.name: Khao phan phak
items.blurb: Thin steamed rice sheets wrapped around blanched veg like cabbage, bean sprouts and morning glory; some shops add egg and minced pork, then ladle hot broth over the top. Rounded, easy flavors that kids take to, and a signature Laplae dish.
items.meta: Breakfast–lunch · Por Khao Phan Phak in town

items.name: Mi phan (Laplae style)
items.blurb: Blanched rice noodles tossed with bean sprouts, lettuce and fried garlic, then rolled in a khao kaep sheet into a long stick. Slightly sweet with a touch of sour, an old local snack.
items.meta: Snack · Pa Wang Mi Phan, Laplae district

items.name: Khao kaep
items.blurb: Thin, crisp rice crackers made from fermented rice flour; eat them on their own or wrapped around mi phan. They keep well and are a favorite Laplae souvenir.

items.name: Long Laplae & Lin Laplae durian
items.blurb: Local durian varieties with smallish fruit, fine dry flesh, shrunken seeds, and a sweet-rich taste. You'll only find them in season at Laplae orchards — the good stuff people drive out to the orchard to taste.

items.name: Laplae langsat & longkong
items.blurb: The town's famous fruit, with clear flesh and a sweet-tart taste kids love. You can pick them fresh from the orchard in season, at better prices than in the big cities.

items.name: Lakeside freshwater fish
items.blurb: Restaurants on the Sirikit Dam crest serve fish straight from the reservoir; order it fried or steamed for easy eating with kids, with the waterside view thrown in.
items.meta: Lunch · lakeside restaurants at Sirikit Dam

blocks.text: Smooth-sailing tips for Uttaradit with kids

items: Your own car is the easiest way — the sights are spread out and public transport within the province is limited, so driving yourself or renting is far more flexible
Pack a change of clothes for the waterfall — the kids will definitely get in the water at Mae Phun; bring towels and non-slip shoes too
Fruit season gets busy — from May to August the orchards and fruit markets are lively, so going a bit early is more relaxed
Bring hats and water — the dam and the waterfall get strong midday sun; kids should wear hats and drink often

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: If your trip is only 2 days, we'd suggest dropping the orchard day and keeping just the dam, the waterfall and the in-town food — that's plenty to keep the kids happy. No need to force every spot in.

faq.q: Is Uttaradit suitable for young kids?
faq.a: Yes, if your family likes nature and relaxed drives. Mae Phun Waterfall is shallow enough for kids to wade in, and Sirikit Dam has plenty of open space to run around. But the town has no theme parks or big rides, so if that's what you're after you may need to adjust your expectations.

faq.q: How many days is right for an Uttaradit family trip?
faq.a: 3 days and 2 nights is about right — it covers the dam, the waterfall, the fruit orchards, an old temple and local food without rushing. If you only have 2 days, you can keep just the dam, the waterfall and the in-town food.

faq.q: When should I visit Uttaradit if I want the kids to taste the fruit?
faq.a: May to August is fruit season, when Long Laplae and Lin Laplae durian, langsat and longkong all come in together and many orchards open to visitors. We'd suggest calling the orchard ahead, since they don't all open at the same time.

faq.q: How far is Sirikit Dam from Uttaradit town?
faq.a: It's in Tha Pla district, about a 1-hour drive from town on good roads with a large parking lot. There are restaurants and cafes on the dam crest, making it a good spot for a full family day out.

faq.q: Can you swim at Mae Phun Waterfall, and is it safe for kids?
faq.a: Yes, you can. Each tier has a shallow pool that isn't very deep, which suits kids. It's open 06:00–17:30. Bring non-slip shoes and keep a close eye on the kids, as the rocks can be slippery after rain.
